text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this huge Premier League fixture as Liverpool welcome Chelsea to Anfield!
It's sure to be an emotional occasion as Liverpool play their first Premier League game since Jurgen Klopp announced that he will leave the club at the end of the season.

The Reds still have a chance of ending his glittering reign on Merseyside with four major trophies, and they enter this contest two points clear of Arsenal at the summit with a game in hand! A huge trip to the Emirates Stadium to face the Gunners is next up for Liverpool, so a victory here to restore their five-point cushion would be huge!

Chelsea finally seem to have discovered some consistency lately, beating Middlesbrough in the EFL Cup semi-finals – to tee up a final meeting with Liverpool – and winning three Premier League games in a row.
Mauricio Pochettino's men would move within nine points of fourth-placed Aston Villa with a victory here – might they still harbour faint hopes of Champions League qualification?

Klopp makes four changes to the Liverpool side which began Sunday's 5-2 FA Cup win over Norwich City, with Mac Allister fit enough to return to the engine room after missing that game with a slight knock.
Szoboszlai returned from injury with a cameo in that match, and he also comes in alongside Van Dijk and Diaz.
Quansah, McConnell, Gravenberch and Gakpo drop to the bench.
Chelsea, meanwhile, make just one change to the XI which began their goalless draw with Aston Villa in the FA Cup on Friday.
Chilwell is the man brought into the lineup as Gilchrist drops to the bench.
Nkunku is among the substitutes after recovering from a hip injury, as is recently recalled midfielder Casadei, but Nicolas Jackson is still unavailable despite Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations exit.
The teams are emerging from the tunnel amid a raucous atmosphere at Anfield! Kick off is fast approaching – what can we expect from these two rivals this time around?
After a predictably rousing rendition of You'll Never Walk Alone, we're under way at Anfield! Szoboszlai gets the ball rolling for Liverpool.
Every game at Anfield between now and the end of the season is likely to be played out amid a party atmosphere as Liverpool bid to give Klopp a triumphant send-off.
His team look to get forward down the right straight from kick-off, but Badiashile gets in front of Bradley to clear.
Palmer sprays a pass in behind for Sterling to chase, but the former Liverpool man just can't reach it as Alisson gets off his line quickly to smother the loose ball.
Good goalkeeping!
Nobody should be surprised if these teams are difficult to separate, with each of their last seven meetings across all competitions finishing level.

It is the longest run of consecutive draws between two top-flight clubs in English football history, and four of the last five have finished goalless (including penalty shootout wins for Liverpool in the 2022 EFL and FA Cup finals).
Let's hope for more entertainment this time around!
Nunez looks to have started centrally for Liverpool, with Diaz to his left and Jota on the right.
The latter looks for Nunez's run in behind but only finds Badiashile, though his rushed clearance gives it straight back to Liverpool.
Unlucky! Bradley sends an Alexander-Arnold-esque pass over the top, with Nunez darting in behind.
Petrovic is caught in no man's land as the Uruguayan attempts to lift a first-time shot over him, but he doesn't get enough power on it and the goalkeeper can retreat to make the save!
PENALTY APPEAL! Sterling is jeered by the home fans as he advances up the left flank before cutting the ball back to Gallagher.

A clever first touch takes Gallagher past his man, then he goes down under Van Dijk's challenge near the six-yard box, but Paul Tierney shakes his head! The VAR has a look in the background... but the incident is cleared – no penalty!
GOOD EFFORT! Nunez goes close! Mac Allister plays a neat one-two with Jota before finding Nunez peeling off the back of Badiashile, and the Uruguayan goes early with his shot from 25 yards out.
It's a powerful strike, and Petrovic has to get his fingertips to it to divert it over the crossbar!
Liverpool fail to make anything of the game's first corner as the Chelsea backline stands firm.
It's been an entertaining first 10 minutes here, featuring two chances for Nunez and a penalty appeal at the other end.
Liverpool are looking dangerous early on! Szoboszlai finds space to sweep a pass out to Diaz,who cuts inside before seeing his shot blocked.
Caicedo then fouls the Colombian after the ball comes back to him, and Liverpool get a free-kick out on the left.
Caicedo, a former Liverpool target, is booked for dissent after that foul.
Wide! Szoboszlai delivers from the free-kick, and though Jota gets across his man to make the first contact, he can't guide his header inside the far post.
Liverpool are on top, though.
Chilwell's pass inside is intercepted by Nunez, and the striker immediately sets his eyes on Petrovic's goal.
This time, however, his 25-yard effort flies well wide of the left-hand post, with the Chelsea goalkeeper untroubled.
Great defending! Bradley sees a right-wing cross cleared and Chelsea break.

The Blues look to have an overload as Palmer slips the ball between the legs of a Liverpool defender, but just as he gets his head up to look for a throughball, Gomez gets back to make a vital challenge and start another Liverpool attack.
Liverpool have had four shots so far in this game, with three of them coming from Nunez.
He looks determined to step up with star forward Mohamed Salah still sidelined.
Chelsea launch a rare counterattack as Gallagher chests the ball away from Mac Allister before finding Madueke.
The winger cuts inside Gomez, but his terrible cross is easily cut out by Van Dijk.
PUSHED ONTO THE POST! Nunez is getting closer! Konate spots Nunez making a run in behind Chelsea's high line and lifts a good pass over the top.

The Uruguayan touches it left before shooting low across goal, and Petrovic dives down to push it against the upright and behind! That's the closest we've come to a goal – Nunez looks up for this one!
With seven goals and six assists, Nunez already has more goal involvements in 20 Premier League appearances this season than he managed in 29 last term (nine goals, three assists).
He was mightily close to another goal there!
Chelsea simply cannot get out at present.
Nunez stands up a cross from the left, and it is only cleared as far as Mac Allister on the edge of the box.
He hammers a shot goalwards, but it clatters off a Blue shirt and behind for a corner.
Petrovic gets up to punch the corner away, but Liverpool keep the attack alive and Bradley lifts a second cross back into the area.
Diaz makes a run across his man to get a glancing header on it, but it spins wide! It's still all Liverpool.
Liverpool have had seven shots, hitting the target three times and creating 0.49 expected goals (xG) in this game.
Chelsea are yet to record an attempt of any kind.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! JOTA MAKES THE BREAKTHROUGH! Liverpool have the goal they deserve as Bradley dispossesses Chilwell before feeding a pass inside to Jota.

He has options right and left, but instead, he charges between Silva and Badiashile, taking advantage of a fortunate ricochet to wriggle through on goal before slotting his finish into the bottom-right corner! 1-0 Liverpool!
Bradley gets the assist, turning defence into attack by dashing over halfway before finding Jota.
The Portugal international had plenty to do, though, and he did it brilliantly!
The VAR has a look at the goal as Chelsea question whether the ball bounced up onto Jota's hand in the build-up, but if anything, it may have hit a Chelsea hand.
The check is over, the goal stands!
Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 86 Premier League games at Anfield when scoring first, winning 77 of those! Chelsea have a real mountain to climb now.
Good defending from Van Dijk, who steps across Madueke to prevent the Chelsea winger from reaching the penalty area before going down and winning a foul.
Liverpool's backline has barely been tested so far.
An update from elsewhere: Liverpool's title rivals Manchester City are 3-0 up at home to Burnley, which means they are set to move level with Arsenal on 46 points.
However, as things stand, Liverpool will restore their five-point buffer to those sides.
We're past the half-hour mark and we've still seen virtually nothing of Chelsea as an attacking force.
Caicedo and Fernandez are involved as the Blues look to calm things down with a spell of patient possession play, but Nunez gets back to recover the ball and get Liverpool moving forward again.

GREAT SAVE! Liverpool are pushing for a second goal, and they almost get one! Jones bends a good effort towards the bottom-right corner from the edge of the box, forcing Petrovic into a strong save down to his left – he had to avoid pushing it straight to Jota.
Bradley whips the ball back into the box, but Nunez sends an acrobatic volley spiralling over the top.
Now Fernandez is cautioned for a late lunge on Jones near the edge of the box.
He joins his midfield partner Caicedo in the book, and Liverpool have a free-kick in a shooting position, perhaps five yards back from the edge of the D.
Szoboszlai stands over the dead ball with usual taker Alexander-Arnold on the bench... but he crashes his effort straight into the wall.
That's poor!
Penalty? No, he's booked for diving! That is embarrassing from Chilwell! The Chelsea left-back drives inside from the wing, beating Konate, who flicks out a foot vaguely in his direction.
He makes absolutely no contact whatsoever, yet Chilwell throws himself down and appeals for a spot-kick.
The referee rightly books him, and he can have no complaints.
Now Chilwell goes down under Bradley's challenge near the corner flag and appeals for a free-kick.
This one probably is a foul, but the referee shakes his head!
Chelsea are starting to enjoy a bit more time on the ball, but they're not threatening Liverpool at all.
Sterling looks to cut inside from the left, but Mac Allister stands his ground and easily recovers possession, much to the pleasure of the home fans.
Klopp has won 199 of his 317 Premier League games in charge of Liverpool.
Victory here, in his 318th match in the competition, would make him the second-fastest manager to 200 Premier League wins, after Pep Guardiola (269 games).
At the moment, his team are cruising.

GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! WHAT A MOMENT FOR BRADLEY! Liverpool have a two-goal lead! Bradley has been absolutely terrific so far, and now he has his first Liverpool goal! Diaz turns and scampers over halfway, with a collision between Jota and Chilwell opening up space on the right.
Sterling doesn't track Bradley as Diaz offloads the ball into the right-back's path, and he drills it across Petrovic and into the bottom-left corner! 2-0 to the Reds!
Diaz gets the assist, darting over halfway before releasing his pass at the perfect time to allow Bradley to rush on and finish across goal.
There's a brief VAR check on the goal to ascertain whether Jota fouled Chilwell off the ball, but it's swiftly cleared! What a moment for Conor Bradley!
Now Disasi is booked for a careless foul, which prompts some complaints from Pochettino.
Chelsea need half-time here.
Liverpool have not let up since going 2-0 up, with Nunez's clever touch giving Jones space to drive down the left-hand side.
He marauds into the half-space before looking for a return pass to Nunez, but it's behind him and runs all the way behind for a goal kick.
Silva slices Jones' cross behind for a Liverpool corner.
Van Dijk heads the deep delivery back across goal, and Chelsea only half clear the danger.
Liverpool will come again!

PENALTY TO LIVERPOOL! Things are going from bad to worse for Chelsea! Gomez lifts a searching ball over the top of Disasi, who slips as Van Dijk – who has stayed up after the corner – brings it down and crosses towards Jota.
The forward's touch takes him across Badiashile, and the Chelsea defender trips him.
That's a spot-kick all day long!
We're into four minutes of stoppage time here, and Liverpool have a chance to go 3-0 up from the spot...
Penalty Miss Darwin Gabriel Núñez Ribeiro
OFF THE POST! Nunez can't convert from 12 yards! Wow.
Jota has to receive treatment after winning the penalty, and as he's temporarily helped from the pitch, Nunez claims the ball.
Petrovic goes the wrong way as Nunez looks for the top-right corner, but his shot bounces off the post and away!
Badiashile must be the most relieved man at Anfield, with Nunez squandering the chance to put Liverpool 3-0 up.
The Uruguayan has now hit the woodwork 11 times in all competitions this season!
Chelsea finally record their first shot as Fernandez takes aim from 25 yards out, but his poor effort bounces straight into the gloves of Alisson.
This first half has been so one-sided.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 CHELSEA.
Paul Tierney blows the half-time whistle, and Chelsea will be mightily relieved to only be 2-0 down.
Liverpool have been utterly dominant from the off here, and Nunez had already rattled the post when they took the lead after 23 minutes.
Sheer force of will took Jota between challenges from Silva and Badiashile, and he calmly slotted past Petrovic.
Young full-back Bradley assisted that goal, and things got even better for him 16 minutes later as he ran onto Diaz's pass before firing across Petrovic and in for his first Liverpool goal.
The Reds had a golden opportunity to go three goals clear when Badiashile conceded a penalty on the stroke of half-time, but Nunez smashed his effort against the woodwork to let them off.
Klopp will be absolutely delighted with Liverpool's first-half performance, while Pochettino will be seething.
Liverpool have had 15 shots to Chelsea's one so far, hitting the target six times and leading the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.87 to 0.02.
The Reds have also had 28 touches in the penalty area to their opponents' three and have managed 39 final-third entries to the Blues' 12.
It's been one-way traffic, and something has to change for Chelsea.
Wow.
Desperate times call for desperate measures, and Pochettino has made a triple substitution at half-time.
Mudryk is on for the ineffective Madueke.
Nkunku makes his return from injury in place of Gallagher.
That move will see Palmer drop into a number 10 role.
Chilwell is perhaps the most surprising withdrawal, though he was booked for diving earlier.
Gusto replaces him.
Chelsea get the ball rolling for the second half.
Is there any way back for the Blues here?
Nunez picks up an early second-half booking for kicking the ball away to prevent a quick Chelsea restart.
Caicedo deflects Jota's pass behind for an early Liverpool corner on the left-hands side.
Szoboszlai delivers, but Silva is up to make the headed clearance.
Chelsea build a rare attack as Caicedo lofts an audacious pass over the top for Sterling.
He's forced to check back as the Blues get men back behind the ball, then his floated cross is comfortably behind Nkunku.
It hasn't been Sterling's day.
Nunez has now hit the woodwork seven times in the Premier League this season, more than twice as many times as any other player.
Two of those came in the first half, when he seemed to do everything but score! Will he get on the scoresheet before the game is through?

WHAT A CHANCE! That is Chelsea's best opportunity of the game by some distance! Gusto – who has come on at right-back with Badiashile switching to the left – darts down the wing before firing a low cross towards Mudryk.
It comes at the substitute quickly, but he has to do better as he balloons his attempt over the crossbar from eight yards out! Alisson was beaten.
Chelsea have won 18 Premier League games against teams starting the day top of the table, more than any other side in the competition’s history.
However, they are winless in their last four such games against Liverpool before this one (one draw, three defeats).
Save! Diaz sees a little reverse pass cut out, but the ball is helped back out to the Colombian by Gomez.
He darts inside Disasi before blasting a shot at goal, but it's too close to Petrovic, who holds it well.
Will Chelsea end up regretting that Mudryk miss? Liverpool have started the second half the way they finished the first, on top.
However, the Blues have carved out a couple of encouraging moments on the break since the restart, without testing Alisson.
Jota has been so lively in this game, and he cuts the ball onto his right foot before drilling a shot into the shins of a defender and behind for a corner.
Szoboszlai's kick is half cleared by Silva, then Liverpool are denied the chance to lift a second cross in as Mac Allister is penalised for handball.
Liverpool are still dominating.

Szoboszlai breezes past Fernandez in the right-hand channel before seeing his cross cleared at the second attempt, but Liverpool recover the loose ball and Bradley cuts inside to win a free-kick perhaps 25 yards from goal, slightly to the right of centre.
Szoboszlai goes for goal from the free-kick... but he hits the wall and his effort loops up onto the roof of the net.
That will be a corner.
It's another underwhelming set-piece from Szoboszlai, which is cleared by the first defender.
Fernandez then cuts out the second cross and sets Sterling off on the break.
Nkunku is demanding an early pass, haring through on goal, but Sterling delays and the Frenchman is caught offside!
Save! Szoboszlai steps over the ball before slipping a reverse pass into Nunez, who gets it out of his feet before bending a shot goalwards from the corner of the box.
Petrovic gets behind it well, and that's nine attempts for Nunez alone in this match!
Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 22 Premier League games at Anfield since suffering a 2-1 defeat against Leeds United in October 2022.
Only Aston Villa (28) have bettered their return of 26 top-flight points won on home soil in 2023-24.
Fortress Anfield looks unlikely to be breached here.
Bradley has been excellent on both sides of the ball here.
He dashes back after Mudryk before stepping across the Ukrainian and being hauled down, winning a free-kick inside his own box.
Great defending!

GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLL! SZOBOSZLAI KILLS THE CONTEST! It's another assist for Bradley! Liverpool take the sting out of the game with a prolonged spell of possession, then Van Dijk hits a booming crossfield ball to Bradley.

He puts his head down and darts down the line, beating Badiashile with ease before lifting a cross onto the edge of the six-yard box, where Szoboszlai plants his header under Petrovic! 3-0 and surely it's game over now!
It's a goal and two assists for Bradley now! He did brilliantly to beat Badiashile and plant his cross right onto the head of Szoboszlai.
What a performance!
Pochettino makes his fourth change after seeing Chelsea go 3-0 down.
Caicedo was booked early on, so he is protected as Chukwuemeka comes on.
It's safe to say that run of seven successive draws between these teams is about to come to an end! Liverpool have been ruthless, and Chelsea look every bit a team in transition.
It could get worse for the Blues yet!
With the points surely secured, Klopp makes four changes in one go! Bradley is the first to go off, and he gets a standing ovation from the home fans as he's replaced by Alexander-Arnold.
A man of the match performance from the 20-year-old!
Jota scored Liverpool's opener, and he is also getting a rest.
Gakpo comes on in attack.
Szoboszlai's goal is one of his final actions as he is also withdrawn, with Klopp protecting him after his return from injury.
Elliot comes on.
Finally, Robertson is brought on for Gomez at left-back.

GOOOOAAALL! CHELSEA GET ONE BACK! Two substitutes combine for Chelsea as they reduce the arrears! Chukwuemeka powers his way to the edge of the box before flicking a pass into Nkunku, who holds off Mac Allister before swivelling to the left and hitting a low shot across Alisson and in off the far post.
They couldn't, could they?
Chukwuemeka gets the assist at the end of a strong run, offloading to Nkunku inside a crowded box.
He did the rest, and that's what Chelsea have been missing during his time on the sidelines.
Chelsea have their tails up now! Another goal for the Blues here would make things very, very interesting!
POSSIBLE PENALTY FOR CHELSEA! Mudryk slips a pass into Nkunku, who holds off Van Dijk with his back to goal before falling under an apparent kick from the defender inside the box.
The referee shakes his head, but the VAR will have a look – Van Dijk appeared to catch the substitute!

NO PENALTY! The VAR check is complete, and the on-pitch decision stands, but that is a bizarre one! Replays show Van Dijk clearly kicked through Nkunku's right foot from behind! Chelsea should have had a penalty, and Pochettino is fuming!

NUNEZ HITS THE WOODWORK AGAIN! OH MY WORD! Nunez leaps to meet a left-wing cross, rising above Badiashile to head goalwards, but he crashes his effort off the crossbar! Liverpool keep the attack alive, and Petrovic makes an awkward save with his legs to deny Elliott! It simply won't go in for Nunez!
Konate is booked for a tactical foul on halfway to prevent a Chelsea break.
What a game we have on our hands here!
Wide! Liverpool come forward again as Gakpo takes aim from 25 yards out, but he doesn't get enough bend on his effort and it just drifts wide to the right of goal.

GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLL! DIAZ MAKES IT 4-1! Nunez may not have a goal to his name, but he does have an assist! Badiashile is playing the Uruguayan onside as he darts onto Mac Allister's throughball before firing a low cross into the six-yard box.
Diaz arrives to steer it past Petrovic, and Liverpool's three-goal cushion is restored!

Nunez has hit the woodwork four times, including from a penalty, and looks destined to end this game without a goal, but he does have an assist! His low cross from the left is perfectly placed for Diaz to convert!
Nunez is the first player on record (since 2003-04) to hit the woodwork four times in a single Premier League match! Hopefully he can take some comfort from that assist for Diaz's goal!
Chelsea briefly threatened a comeback, and they were extremely unfortunate to be denied a penalty shortly after Nkunku made it 3-1, but they look a beaten side now.
Liverpool have been electric going forward and have looked like they could score at will.
Klopp makes his fifth and final change as Clark replaces Jones.
Nunez spins outside the box before looking for goal again... but it's a weak effort which rolls straight to Petrovic.
The Uruguayan has now attempted 11 of Liverpool's 28 shots in this match – Chelsea have recorded four as a team!
We're going to see a Chelsea debut for former Leicester City loanee Casadei.
He replaces Palmer, who has been totally anonymous, for the closing stages.
Mac Allister stays down, holding his knee, following a collision with Casadei near the edge of the Chelsea box.
The Argentine needs treatment here.
Mac Allister is back on his feet and looks capable of carrying on, though he has to temporarily leave the field as the game restarts.
Only Bukayo Saka (12) has more assists among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Liverpool's Nunez (11).
Can he cap a typically chaotic performance with a goal in the closing minutes?
We're into six minutes of stoppage time here! Liverpool are just keeping the ball patiently now, with no need to force the issue at 4-1 up.
Save! Liverpool are still chasing a fifth goal here, with Nunez bringing down a long ball on his chest before finding Gakpo inside him.
The substitute shoots low towards the bottom-left corner, but it's a routine stop for Petrovic.
It's going to be back to the drawing board for Pochettino after this game.

He could have become the first Chelsea boss to oversee four straight Premier League wins since Thomas Tuchel in 2022, but instead, his team could drop into the bottom half on Thursday, depending on Wolves' result against Manchester United!
Chelsea win a late corner on the left as they bid to make the scoreline more respectable, but Alisson gets up to punch Mudryk's cross away before Sterling fouls Clark.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-1 CHELSEA.
It's full-time at Anfield, and Liverpool restore their five-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a crushing 4-1 win over Chelsea.

The Reds were utterly dominant in the first half with Jota and Bradley finding the net before Nunez missed a penalty, and that didn't change after the restart! Szoboszlai headed in Liverpool's third as Bradley recorded his second assist of a man-of-the-match performance, though Chelsea briefly threatened a fightback when Nkunku came on to reduce the arrears before seeing a decent penalty appeal turned down.

However, Liverpool went back on the attack and Nunez – who hit the woodwork a Premier League-record four times throughout the game – teed up a fourth strike from Diaz as the Reds ran out dominant winners.

They now go to Arsenal for a titanic top-of-the-table tussle on Sunday, while Chelsea must banish this result ahead of a home game against Wolves, who could be above them by the time that match kicks off! That's all from Anfield, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
